title: Ecclesiasticus 18: do not wait until death to be justified
source_text: VII. Neque etiam quadrat sensus forensis loco qui habetur Ecclesiastici cap. 18. vers. 22. Ne expectes usque ad mortem justificari. Ubi scopus scriptoris est homines monere ut resipiscant, & probi sanctique fiant per verum ac syncerum pietatis studium. Unde est quod verba illa vernacula nostra vertit, Nattendez point a estre homme de bien jusqua la mort.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does the forensic sense fit the place in Ecclesiasticus chapter 18 verse 22: Do not wait until death to be justified. Where the writer's aim is to warn men to repent, and to become upright and holy through a true and sincere pursuit of piety. Whence it is that our vernacular renders those words, Do not wait to be a good man until death.
pass_b_english: Ecclus 18:22 resists a bare forensic gloss.
Aim: repent and become holy now—vernacular: do not wait till death to be good.
